messages.content: 你能計算我進行的科學實驗中空氣在恆壓下的熱容量嗎？我有一個容積為2.5立方公尺的容器，並能保持溫度在300開氏度。我將在更高的溫度350開氏度重複這個實驗，接下來在更低的容積1.5立方公尺下一樣重複這個實驗。我在所有這些實驗中都使用空氣。你能提供這三種不同條件下的熱容量嗎？

function.name: calc_heat_capacity
function.description: Calculate the heat capacity at constant pressure of air using its temperature and volume. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

temp.description: The temperature of the gas in Kelvin.

volume.description: The volume of the gas in m^3. This is a float type value.

gas.description: Type of gas, with air as default.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate heat capacity at constant pressure of air given temp and volume. But heat capacity at constant pressure (Cp) for ideal gas depends only on temperature, not volume. For air, Cp ~ 1005 J/(kg·K) at room temperature, but can vary slightly with temperature. We can approximate using ideal gas constant R=8.314 J/(mol·K), molar mass M_air ~ 28.97 g/mol. Cp,molar ~ 29.1 J/(mol·K). Actually Cp,molar for air ~ 29.1 J/(mol·K). So Cp per kg ~ Cp,molar / M_air * 1000? Wait: Cp per mole = 29.1 J/(mol·K). Molar mass 28.97 g/mol = 0.02897 kg/mol. So Cp per kg = Cp_molar / M_mol = 29.1 / 0.02897 ≈ 1004 J/(kg·K). Good.

But we might want to compute heat capacity of the amount of air in the container: C = Cp * mass. Mass = density * volume. Density of air at 300 K and 1 atm ~ 1.177 kg/m3. At 350 K ~ 1.013 kg/m3. But we can approximate using ideal gas law: PV = nRT => n = PV/(RT). Mass = n*M_mol. So mass = (P*V*M_mol)/(R*T). Then C = Cp * mass. So we can compute for each condition.

Assume P=1 atm = 101325 Pa. R=8.314 J/(mol·K). M_mol=0.02897 kg/mol. Cp per mole = 29.1 J/(mol·K). So Cp per kg = 1004 J/(kg·K). But we can also compute C per mole: Cp_molar = 29.1 J/(mol·K). So C_total = Cp_molar * n. That yields same result.

Let's compute:

Case1: V=2.5 m3, T=300 K. n = P*V/(R*T) = 101325*2.5/(8.314*300) = (253312.5)/(2494.2) ≈ 101.5 mol? Let's compute precisely: 101325*2.5 = 253312.5. Divide by (8.314*300)=2494.2. 253312.5/2494.2 ≈ 101.5. So n≈101.5 mol. C_total = Cp_molar*n = 29.1*101.5 ≈ 2955 J/K. Alternatively mass = n*M_mol = 101.5*0.02897=2.94 kg. Cp per kg=1004 => C_total=1004*2.94=2955 J/K. Good.

Case2: V=2.5 m3, T=350 K. n = 101325*2.5/(8.314*350)=253312.5/(2910.9)=87.1 mol. C_total=29.1*87.1=2535 J/K. Mass=87.1*0.02897=2.52 kg. C_total=1004*2.52=2535 J/K.

Case3: V=1.5 m3, T=300 K. n=101325*1.5/(8.314*300)=151687.5/2494.2=60.8 mol. C_total=29.1*60.8=1770 J/K. Mass=60.8*0.02897=1.76 kg. C_total=1004*1.76=1767 J/K.

So results: 2955 J/K, 2535 J/K, 1770 J/K.

We should call the function calc_heat_capacity. Provide temp and volume. The function expects temp in Kelvin, volume in m^3, gas optional. We'll call it three times. Use default gas "air". We'll pass temp=300, volume=2.5; temp=350, volume=2.5; temp=300, volume=1.5. We'll get outputs. Let's do that.
